title: The Honest DSL with Hannah Carter
author: Hannah Carter
source: Thinking Deeply about Primary Education, December 29, 2025
summary: Hannah Carter's episode on the Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) role moves beyond statutory guidance to explore the lived experience of school leaders tasked with safeguarding. Rather than reiterating policy, Carter focuses on the accumulation of incidents, the emotional residue of the role, and how safeguarding thinking follows DSLs home. The conversation is rare in acknowledging what the role actually does to the person performing it—the quiet toll of managing child protection concerns, navigating complex systems, and carrying the weight of responsibility. For leaders and senior staff who support or sit in the DSL role, this episode offers honest reflection on the profession as it is lived, not as it appears in policy documents. The episode is part of the larger Thinking Deeply about Primary Education series focused on meaningful professional development.
points: Safeguarding training typically focuses on what to do; Carter's work addresses what the safeguarding role does to the person doing it.
The emotional accumulation of incident management, investigation support, and child protection concerns creates a form of professional toll that isn't acknowledged in formal training.
DSL thinking often follows school leaders home, affecting their personal wellbeing and family life in ways that policy frameworks don't anticipate.
Honest conversation about the DSL role requires acknowledging the complexity of working with idiosyncratic humans, child welfare systems, and organizational constraints simultaneously.
Senior leaders who support DSLs benefit from understanding the lived reality of the role rather than treating it as a checklist of statutory duties.
quotes: Safeguarding training often tells us what to do. Far less often does it acknowledge what the role does to the person doing it.

This week's episode is a quietly powerful conversation with Hannah Carter, author of The Honest DSL. Rather than revisiting statutory guidance, we focus on the lived experience of being a Designated Safeguarding Lead.
If you lead safeguarding, support a DSL, or sit in senior leadership, this episode offers something rare: an honest account of the role as it is actually lived, not as it appears in policy documents.
The accumulation of incidents, the emotional residue, and the way safeguarding thinking can follow you home.
The Honest DSL offers strategies for Designated Safeguarding Leads navigating the complex human and systemic realities of child protection work in schools.
